business: Cyra Health, a private PCOS and irregular-cycle tracking app (iOS, Android, web)
by_segment: Student or early-career with irregular periods
why_not: The no-account, stays-on-my-phone part actually gets me to download it, but the doctor PDF is the thing I'd use and that's free. Pro is an AI chat and breathing exercises, and I'm not paying to send my log to an AI when what I want is to know if my inositol is working.

Honestly the free version is the part I want: ranges instead of a fake 28-day guess and a PDF I can show my doctor. I'd download it and try it, but I'm not paying $5 a month on my budget for an AI write-up when I don't know yet if the free predictions are any better than Flo's.

I'd maybe download the free version, since honest ranges instead of a fake 28-day guess and the doctor PDF actually sound useful. But I don't pay for apps, and an AI write-up of my own notes isn't worth $5 a month when Apple Health and my Notes app cost nothing.

I'd maybe download the free version for the doctor PDF, but I've quit every tracker within a few weeks because logging feels like homework, so paying for Pro before I've even stuck with the free part makes no sense. An AI write-up of my own log doesn't tell me whether my metformin is working or change what my doctor does.

I'd download the free version, because on-phone storage with no account is exactly what I want, and the doctor PDF could help me find out whether the metformin is doing anything. But I won't pay to send my fertility log to an AI until I've read the privacy policy and seen who handles that data, and I'd want a couple of months of free use before I decide Pro is worth it.

I might download the free version for the doctor PDF, since my period is six weeks late and I need something to show a clinician, but I'm not paying to have my log sent to an AI. On $31k, five bucks a month for a chatbot and breathing exercises isn't a priority.

I'd download the free version for the doctor-ready PDF because that's exactly my problem before appointments, but I never pay for apps and nothing in Pro is something I need. An AI write-up and breathing exercises aren't worth $5 a month when the free part already does the job.

I might download the free version for the doctor PDF since that's my actual problem, but I don't pay for apps, period. An AI write-up of my own log isn't worth $5 a month when I can just read it myself before my appointment.
flip: If the free version actually got my cycles roughly right for a few months and the AI summary helped me get a doctor to take me seriously and order PCOS tests, I might pay for a year once, at a deal.
If my doctor actually used the Pro write-up and it helped get my fertility questions taken seriously, maybe a one-time payment, but not a monthly one.
If I actually kept logging for a couple of months on the free version and the doctor PDF got my doctor to change something, like adjusting my meds or ordering tests, I'd consider paying.

If Pro showed me a before-and-after of my symptoms and cycle length since I started metformin or inositol, in a form my doctor would take seriously, so it saves me an appointment or gets me a real answer faster.

If after a few months the free ranges were actually right for me and the Pro write-up could clearly show whether my metformin or inositol is changing my cycles or symptoms, I'd pay for the yearly plan.

If I'd actually kept logging on the free version for two or three months and Pro gave me something concrete for trying to conceive, like ovulation likelihood with PCOS or something my OB said was useful, not just AI commentary.
If my doctor actually used the Pro write-up and it changed what happened at my appointment, I might pay for a month or two around visits.

Proof that the doctor-ready report actually changed how clinicians treated people, plus an independent privacy audit showing what the AI part sends and that it isn't kept.
